correctness.rationale: The support of any independent double Roman function is independent and no support vertex can have label 1. In a rook graph an independent support is a partial matching. Defense of every zero implies domination, forcing the matching to saturate the smaller board dimension. Square boards then give two support neighbors at each zero and minimum label 2 throughout; unequal boards have an unoccupied column, so every row contains a zero with exactly one support neighbor and that support must be label 3. This yields the formula and complete minimum families. Direct exhaustive checking confirms all minima on R_2,2, R_2,3, and R_3,3.

value.rationale: Rectangular rook graphs are a standard family simultaneously representable as Cartesian products and line graphs of complete bipartite graphs. The exact formula has a sharp equal-versus-unequal phase, and the complete minimum families are classical permutation/injection objects. The result therefore provides a natural benchmark for how the double-defense condition interacts with independent matching support, rather than an arbitrary finite slice.
